exams.title: COMP6080 Sprint Paper 03
exams.description: A final sprint paper that deliberately avoids the mechanisms already drilled in the other papers. It focuses on the least-covered material: React fundamentals (mounting, props, children, the style object, CSS Modules), one Week 7 module-boundary question, and four Week 8 questions on delivery, UI testing, rendering strategies and tooling. Ten questions, three sub-questions each, with screenshot-style mockups.
exams.descriptionZh: 一套刻意避开其他整卷已反复考查机制的总复习冲刺卷。重点放在目前覆盖最少的材料：React 基础（挂载、props、children、style 对象、CSS Modules）、一道 Week 7 的模块职责边界题，以及四道 Week 8 题，分别关于交付、UI 测试、渲染策略与工程工具。共 10 道大题，每题 3 个子题，配套截图感 mockup。

questions.title: The app that mounts nothing
questions.contentMdx:
A small React app is split across `index.html` and `main.jsx`. The HTML page contains `
`, but `main.jsx` calls `createRoot(document.getElementById('root'))`. When the page loads the console shows `Uncaught Error: createRoot(...): Target container is not a DOM element.` and nothing renders. `screen.png` shows the blank page.
questions.contentMdxZh:
一个小的 React 应用拆在 `index.html` 与 `main.jsx` 两个文件里。HTML 页面里是 `
`，但 `main.jsx` 调用的是 `createRoot(document.getElementById('root'))`。页面加载后控制台报 `Uncaught Error: createRoot(...): Target container is not a DOM element.`，什么也没渲染出来。`screen.png` 展示了这张空白页。

subQuestions.label: (a)
subQuestions.questionMdx: What does `document.getElementById('root')` return on this page, and why does `createRoot(...)` fail with it?
subQuestions.answerMdx: The markup only has an element with `id="app"`, so no element has the id `root`. `document.getElementById('root')` therefore returns `null`. `createRoot` needs a real DOM element to use as the container it will render into; given `null` it has nothing to attach to and throws `Target container is not a DOM element`.
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for identifying that `getElementById('root')` returns `null` because no element carries that id.
1 mark for stating `createRoot` needs a real DOM element as its container and throws when it gets `null`.
subQuestions.questionMdxZh: 在这个页面上 `document.getElementById('root')` 会返回什么？为什么 `createRoot(...)` 会因此报错？
subQuestions.answerMdxZh: 标记里只有一个 `id="app"` 的元素，没有任何元素的 id 是 `root`，所以 `document.getElementById('root')` 返回 `null`。`createRoot` 需要一个真实的 DOM 元素作为它的容器（也就是渲染落点）；拿到 `null` 就没有可挂载的对象，于是抛出 `Target container is not a DOM element`。
subQuestions.markingMdxZh:
1 分：指出 `getElementById('root')` 返回 `null`，因为没有元素带这个 id。
1 分：说明 `createRoot` 需要一个真实 DOM 元素作为容器，拿到 `null` 就会报错。

subQuestions.label: (b)
subQuestions.questionMdx: Explain the relationship between the id written in the HTML and the `getElementById` call, and what the "root" container is for React.
subQuestions.answerMdx: The `id` in the HTML names an element; `getElementById` looks that name up in the current document and returns the matching element, or `null` if none matches. The two strings must agree character for character — `app` and `root` are different names, so the lookup misses. The root container is the one existing DOM node that React takes over: React mounts its component tree inside it and re-renders into it. Everything React draws lives under that container, so when the lookup fails there is no place to mount and the app never starts.
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for explaining that the HTML id and the `getElementById` argument must match exactly.
1 mark for describing the root as the existing DOM node React mounts its component tree into.
1 mark for linking a failed lookup to there being no container, so nothing renders.
subQuestions.questionMdxZh: 请说明 HTML 里写的 id 与 `getElementById` 调用之间的关系，并说明 React 所说的 “root” 容器是什么。
subQuestions.answerMdxZh: HTML 里的 `id` 是给某个元素起的名字；`getElementById` 在当前文档里按这个名字查找，返回匹配到的元素，找不到就返回 `null`。两个字符串必须逐字符一致——`app` 和 `root` 是两个不同的名字，所以查找落空。root 容器就是 React 接管的那一个已存在的 DOM 节点：React 把组件树挂载到它里面，并把更新渲染进它里面。React 画出的所有内容都活在这个容器之下，所以查找一旦失败就没有挂载落点，应用根本起不来。
subQuestions.markingMdxZh:
1 分：说明 HTML 中的 id 与 `getElementById` 的参数必须完全一致。
1 分：把 root 描述为 React 把组件树挂载进去的那个已存在的 DOM 节点。
1 分：把查找失败与 “没有容器、所以什么都不渲染” 联系起来。

subQuestions.label: (c)
subQuestions.questionMdx: Give the fix, and explain what happens if the module script runs before the target element exists.
subQuestions.answerMdx:
Make the two names agree — either change the HTML to `
` or change the call to `createRoot(document.getElementById('app'))` — then `root.render()` mounts into that element. If the module script runs before the element exists in the DOM, the lookup still returns `null` and the same error is thrown; the element must already be parsed when `createRoot` runs (place the script after the element, or use `defer` or a module that waits for the DOM).
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for making the id in the HTML and the lookup match (either side).
1 mark for showing `root.render(<App />)` mounts into that container.
1 mark for stating the element must already exist at run time, otherwise the lookup is `null` and mounting fails again.
subQuestions.questionMdxZh: 请给出改法，并说明如果模块脚本在目标元素出现之前就执行，会发生什么。
subQuestions.answerMdxZh:
让两个名字一致即可——要么把 HTML 改成 `
`，要么把调用改成 `createRoot(document.getElementById('app'))`，然后 `root.render()` 就会挂载进该元素。如果模块脚本在目标元素还没进入 DOM 时就执行，查找仍会返回 `null`，同一个错误会再次抛出；`createRoot` 运行时该元素必须已经被解析（把脚本放到元素之后，或使用 `defer`，或让模块等到 DOM 就绪）。
subQuestions.markingMdxZh:
1 分：让 HTML 中的 id 与查找参数一致（改任意一侧）。
1 分：展示 `root.render(<App />)` 挂载进该容器。
1 分：说明运行时该元素必须已经存在，否则查找为 `null`，挂载再次失败。

questions.title: The count that forgets the click
questions.contentMdx: `Counter.jsx` receives its value from the parent as a prop and tries to add to it inside the click handler by writing to `props.value`. Each click logs a larger number in the console, but the button label never changes, and any later render puts the old value back. `counter.png` shows the frozen label.
questions.contentMdxZh: `Counter.jsx` 从父组件以 prop 的形式拿到值，并试图在点击处理器里通过给 `props.value` 赋值来累加。每次点击控制台都会打印一个更大的数字，但按钮上的文字始终不变，之后任何一次渲染又会把旧值写回去。`counter.png` 展示了这个 “冻结” 的标签。

subQuestions.label: (a)
subQuestions.questionMdx: Why does the label stay the same after a click even though the console logs a larger number?
subQuestions.answerMdx: The handler only writes to the `props` object of the current render; it never asks React to render again. React re-renders in response to state changes, and nothing here changed any state, so no new render happens and the visible label keeps the old prop value. The `console.log` shows the mutated object in memory, which is not what the screen is showing.
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for stating the handler never triggers a re-render because no state changed.
1 mark for stating the screen keeps the previously rendered value, so the log (a mutated object) differs from what is shown.
subQuestions.questionMdxZh: 明明控制台打印了更大的数字，为什么点击后标签还是不变？
subQuestions.answerMdxZh: 该处理器只是写了本次渲染的 `props` 对象，并没有请求 React 再渲染一次。React 是因 state 变化而重新渲染的，而这里没有任何 state 改变，所以不会发生新的渲染，屏幕上的标签仍保留上一次渲染出的旧 prop 值。`console.log` 打印的是内存里被改动的对象，它并不等于屏幕正在显示的内容。
subQuestions.markingMdxZh:
1 分：说明处理器没有触发重渲染，因为没有任何 state 变化。
1 分：说明屏幕仍是上一次渲染的值，所以日志（被改动的对象）与所显示的内容不一致。

subQuestions.label: (b)
subQuestions.questionMdx: Whose data is it, and what is a child component allowed to do with a prop it does not own? How is a child supposed to signal a change?
subQuestions.answerMdx: The prop is the parent's data passed down read-only; the parent owns the value and the child only reads it. React's one-way data flow means a child must not modify a prop — props are a component's inputs, like function arguments. To change the value, the child calls a function the parent passed down (for example `onIncrement`), which changes the parent's state; the parent then re-renders the child with the new prop value. The child requests a change; the owner performs it.
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for stating the prop belongs to the parent and is read-only for the child.
1 mark for explaining one-way data flow: mutating a prop is not allowed.
1 mark for describing the child calling a parent-provided callback, so the owner updates state and re-renders with the new value.
subQuestions.questionMdxZh: 这份数据是谁的？子组件对不属于自己的 prop 能做什么？子组件应当如何发出 “我要改” 的信号？
subQuestions.answerMdxZh: prop 是父组件传下来的数据，对子组件而言是只读的；父组件拥有这个值，子组件只能读。React 的单向数据流意味着子组件不得修改 prop——props 是组件的输入，就像函数的参数。要改变这个值，子组件应调用父组件传下来的函数（例如 `onIncrement`），由它去改父组件的 state；父组件随后带着新的 prop 值重新渲染子组件。子组件负责 “请求改动”，拥有者负责 “执行改动”。
subQuestions.markingMdxZh:
1 分：说明 prop 属于父组件，对子组件是只读的。
1 分：解释单向数据流——不允许修改 prop。
1 分：说明子组件调用父组件传入的回调，让拥有者更新 state 并以新值重渲染。

subQuestions.label: (c)
subQuestions.questionMdx: Rewrite Counter so it follows the contract, and explain why mutating props is a bug even when the number sometimes looks right.
subQuestions.answerMdx: Give the parent a `useState` for the count and pass both the value and a callback: parent `const [count, setCount] = useState(0); <Counter value={count} onIncrement={() => setCount(count + 1)} />`; child `function Counter({ value, onIncrement }) { return <button onClick={onIncrement}>Count: {value}</button> }`. Now a click calls the parent's setter, state changes, and React re-renders with the new value. Mutating a prop is a bug because it edits another component's data without a re-render and desynchronises the DOM from the model; the number only "looks right" in a local log, until the next render overwrites it.
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for keeping the value in the parent's `useState`.
1 mark for passing a callback (e.g. `onIncrement`) that calls the parent setter.
1 mark for explaining that mutating a prop bypasses the re-render and desynchronises the model from the DOM.
subQuestions.questionMdxZh: 请按这套契约重写 Counter，并解释为什么 “修改 props” 是 Bug——即便那个数字有时看起来是对的。
subQuestions.answerMdxZh: 在父组件里用 `useState` 保存计数，同时把值和回调一起传下去：父组件 `const [count, setCount] = useState(0); <Counter value={count} onIncrement={() => setCount(count + 1)} />`；子组件 `function Counter({ value, onIncrement }) { return <button onClick={onIncrement}>Count: {value}</button> }`。这样点击会调用父组件的 setter，state 变化后 React 用新值重渲染。修改 prop 之所以是 Bug，是因为它在不触发重渲染的情况下改了另一个组件的数据，让 DOM 与模型失同步；那个数字只是在一个局部日志里 “看起来对”，下一次渲染就会把它覆盖掉。
subQuestions.markingMdxZh:
1 分：把值保存在父组件的 `useState` 里。
1 分：传下一个调用父组件 setter 的回调（如 `onIncrement`）。
1 分：说明修改 prop 绕过了重渲染，使模型与 DOM 失同步。

questions.title: The card that was copied three times
questions.contentMdx: `Card.jsx` hardcodes its body (a heading and a paragraph). The team also needed the same frame for a report panel and a tip panel, so they duplicated the whole component twice. A single border change now has to be made in three places. `cards.png` shows the three identical frames.
questions.contentMdxZh: `Card.jsx` 把内容写死在里面（一个标题加一段文字）。团队后来又需要同样的外框来做 “报告面板” 和 “提示面板”，于是把整个组件复制了两份。现在只要改一次边框，就得改三个地方。`cards.png` 展示了这三个一模一样的外框。

subQuestions.label: (a)
subQuestions.questionMdx: What is `props.children`, and what does it let Card do that a hardcoded body cannot?
subQuestions.answerMdx: `props.children` is whatever you place between a component's opening and closing tags — the nested JSX React passes to the component as a prop. It lets the component own a fixed frame while the caller supplies the inside, so one Card can wrap a heading, a list, a form or a tip without being rewritten. A hardcoded body can only ever render the one thing written inside it.
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for defining `props.children` as the JSX placed between the component's tags.
1 mark for stating it lets the caller supply the content while the component keeps a fixed frame.
subQuestions.questionMdxZh: `props.children` 是什么？它让 Card 能做到哪些写死内容做不到的事？
subQuestions.answerMdxZh: `props.children` 就是你在组件开始标签和结束标签之间放的内容——React 把这部分嵌套 JSX 作为 prop 传给组件。它让组件保留一个固定的外框，而由调用方提供内部内容，于是同一个 Card 就能承载标题、列表、表单或提示，而不必重写。写死内容的话，永远只能渲染里面写的那一样东西。
subQuestions.markingMdxZh:
1 分：把 `props.children` 定义为放在组件标签之间的 JSX。
1 分：说明它让调用方提供内容，而组件保留固定外框。

subQuestions.label: (b)
subQuestions.questionMdx: Explain the separation of responsibility this creates, and what "composition" means here.
subQuestions.answerMdx: Card becomes responsible only for the frame (border, padding, layout) and stays the same for every use; the caller becomes responsible for the content it passes in. This is composition: building bigger screens by nesting small, single-purpose components rather than by adding options or copy-pasting. Because the frame lives in one definition, a change to it appears everywhere it is used, and Card stays reusable for content it has never seen.
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for stating Card owns the frame and the caller owns the content.
1 mark for naming this "composition" (nesting small components to build bigger UI).
1 mark for noting the frame is defined once, so changes propagate and Card stays reusable.
subQuestions.questionMdxZh: 请说明这样形成的职责划分，以及这里的 “组合（composition）” 指什么。
subQuestions.answerMdxZh: Card 只负责外框（边框、内边距、布局），在每次使用时都保持不变；调用方则负责它传进去的内容。这就是组合（composition）：通过把小而专一的组件嵌套起来搭出更大的界面，而不是靠加选项或复制粘贴。由于外框只有一处定义，改一次就会体现在所有使用它的地方，Card 也能用来承载它从未见过的新内容。
subQuestions.markingMdxZh:
1 分：说明 Card 负责外框、调用方负责内容。
1 分：点出这是 “组合”（通过嵌套小组件搭建更大的 UI）。
1 分：指出外框只定义一次，改动会自动传播，Card 保持可复用。

questions.title: The badge that never turns red
questions.titleZh: 永远变不成红色的徽标
questions.contentMdx: `Badge.jsx` sets its look with an inline `style` object. `padding: 6` takes effect, but `background-color` and `border-radius` do nothing — every badge keeps the browser default. `badge.png` shows a high-priority badge that ignored the red.
questions.contentMdxZh: `Badge.jsx` 用一个内联 `style` 对象来设定外观。`padding: 6` 生效了，但 `background-color` 和 `border-radius` 毫无效果——每个徽标都保持浏览器默认样式。`badge.png` 展示了一个本该是红色的高优先级徽标。

subQuestions.label: (a)
subQuestions.questionMdx: Why does `padding: 6` apply but `background-color` does not?
subQuestions.answerMdx: React's `style` prop is a JavaScript object, and its keys must be the JavaScript property names (camelCase), so `padding` is a valid key and is applied. `background-color` is a CSS property name, not a JavaScript one; React does not recognise that key, skips it, and warns `Unsupported style property background-color. Did you mean backgroundColor?` in development. The declaration is dropped, so the background never changes.
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for stating the style object uses JavaScript (camelCase) property names, so `padding` is valid and applied.
1 mark for stating `background-color` is not a recognised key, so it is ignored (with a warning).
subQuestions.questionMdxZh: 为什么 `padding: 6` 能生效，而 `background-color` 却不能？
subQuestions.answerMdxZh: React 的 `style` prop 是一个 JavaScript 对象，它的键必须是 JavaScript 属性名（小驼峰），所以 `padding` 是合法的键，会被应用。`background-color` 是 CSS 属性名而不是 JavaScript 属性名；React 不认识这个键，会跳过它，并在开发模式下警告 `Unsupported style property background-color. Did you mean backgroundColor?`。这条声明被丢弃，背景自然没有变化。
subQuestions.markingMdxZh:
1 分：说明 style 对象使用 JavaScript（小驼峰）属性名，所以 `padding` 合法并生效。
1 分：说明 `background-color` 不是被识别的键，因此被忽略（并给出警告）。

subQuestions.label: (b)
subQuestions.questionMdx: Why are the keys JavaScript property names rather than CSS property names, and what does React do with a key it does not recognise?
subQuestions.answerMdx: In an inline style React does not write CSS text; it sets properties on the element's `style` object in JavaScript, and that object's properties are camelCase (identifiers cannot contain dashes). So React expects `backgroundColor`, `borderRadius`, `fontSize`, and so on. When it meets an unknown key it cannot map it to a `style` property, so it ignores the declaration — the element keeps its previous value — and logs a warning in development. The style silently "does not work" rather than throwing.
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for explaining that React sets properties on the JavaScript `style` object, whose properties are camelCase.
1 mark for naming the correct keys (e.g. `backgroundColor`, `borderRadius`).
1 mark for stating an unknown key is ignored (with a warning), so the declaration silently has no effect.
subQuestions.questionMdxZh: 为什么这些键用的是 JavaScript 属性名而不是 CSS 属性名？React 遇到不认识的键会怎么处理？
subQuestions.answerMdxZh: 对于内联样式，React 并不是在写 CSS 文本，而是在 JavaScript 里给元素的 `style` 对象设置属性，而这个对象上的属性是小驼峰命名（标识符里不能带连字符）。所以 React 期望的是 `backgroundColor`、`borderRadius`、`fontSize` 等等。当它遇到不认识的键时，无法把它映射到 `style` 属性上，就会忽略这条声明——元素保持之前的值——并在开发模式下打印警告。样式是 “悄悄失效”，而不是抛错。
subQuestions.markingMdxZh:
1 分：说明 React 给 JavaScript 的 `style` 对象设置属性，其属性名为小驼峰。
1 分：给出正确的键名（如 `backgroundColor`、`borderRadius`）。
1 分：说明不认识的键会被忽略（并警告），声明悄无声息地失效。

subQuestions.questionMdx: Rewrite the style so every declaration applies, and explain the rule for numbers.

questions.contentMdx: `Card.jsx` and `Button.jsx` each import a plain `.css` file, and both render `className="title"`. `Card.css` wants a large, dark title; `Button.css` wants a small, light one. subQuestions.questionMdx: Why do two components that both use `className="title"` end up sharing one style?
subQuestions.answerMdx: A plain `.css` import is global: the selector `.title` is added to the whole document, not scoped to the file that imported it. So both components' elements match the same `title` rule set, and with equal specificity the declaration that appears later in the cascade wins for both. The class name is a shared global handle, so the two components cannot have different `title` styles.

1 分：说明普通 CSS 引入是全局的，`.title` 作用于整个文档。
1 分：说明优先级相同时，靠后的规则对两个组件都生效。

subQuestions.label: (b)

subQuestions.answerMdxZh: 类名是实现的细节——一个样式句柄，它可以在用户所见、所能做的都没有变化的情况下被改掉。把测试绑定到精确的字符串，意味着一次无害的重构（改类名）就会让测试失败，制造误报。与此同时，它对行为只字未提，所以真正的 Bug——点击后总价不再更新——反而能通过测试，因为类名还是对的。
subQuestions.markingMdxZh:
1 分：说明类名是实现的细节，可以在用户无感的情况下变化。
1 分：说明这会让测试在无害重构时失败，却漏掉真正的行为 Bug。

subQuestions.label: (b)
subQuestions.questionMdx: Explain the difference between testing implementation details and testing user-visible behaviour, and which survives a refactor.
subQuestions.answerMdx: An implementation test asserts on internals: class names, component names, internal state, or exact markup structure. A behaviour test describes what a user can see and do — the text on screen, an accessible name, or the result of clicking — which is the contract of the feature. Behaviour survives refactors because renaming a class, changing a wrapper element or moving code does not change the visible outcome, so the test keeps passing while still failing if the outcome actually breaks. Implementation tests tend to break on refactors and miss behaviour bugs at the same time.
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for defining an implementation test (class names, internal state, exact markup) versus a behaviour test (what the user sees or does).
1 mark for stating behaviour survives refactors because the visible outcome is unchanged.
1 mark for noting implementation tests break on refactors and miss behaviour bugs at the same time.
subQuestions.questionMdxZh: 请说明 “测实现细节” 与 “测用户可见行为” 的区别，以及哪一种能在重构后存活。
subQuestions.answerMdxZh: 测实现细节，断言的是内部构造：类名、组件名、内部 state，或精确的标记结构。测行为，描述的是用户能看到、能做到的事——屏幕上的文字、可访问名称、点击后的结果——这才是该功能的契约。行为测试能在重构后存活：改类名、换一层包裹元素、挪动代码都不会改变可见结果，于是测试继续通过，而一旦结果真的坏掉它就会失败。实现测试则往往在重构时崩掉，同时还漏掉行为 Bug。
subQuestions.markingMdxZh:
1 分：定义实现测试（类名、内部 state、精确标记）与行为测试（用户所见/所做）。
1 分：说明行为测试因可见结果不变而能熬过重构。
1 分：指出实现测试既会在重构时崩掉，又会漏掉行为 Bug。

subQuestions.label: (c)
subQuestions.questionMdx: Rewrite the test to assert what the user can see and do.
subQuestions.answerMdx: Query by role and accessible name, then assert on the visible result: `const button = screen.getByRole('button', { name: /add to cart/i }); await userEvent.click(button); expect(screen.getByText('Total: $15.00')).toBeInTheDocument()`. The test no longer mentions the class, so a rename cannot break it; it checks the button's accessible name (also a small accessibility check) and that clicking actually updates the total, which is the behaviour a regression would break.
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for querying by role and accessible name instead of a class.
1 mark for performing a user action (clicking) and asserting on a visible result.
1 mark for explaining the test now survives a rename and would catch the total no longer updating.
subQuestions.questionMdxZh: 请把测试改成断言用户能看到和能做到的事情。
subQuestions.answerMdxZh: 按角色与可访问名称来查询，然后断言可见的结果：`const button = screen.getByRole('button', { name: /add to cart/i }); await userEvent.click(button); expect(screen.getByText('Total: $15.00')).toBeInTheDocument()`。测试不再提到类名，所以改名就无法让它失败；它检查按钮的可访问名称（顺带做了一次小小的可访问性检查），并检查点击确实更新了总价——这正是回归会破坏的行为。
subQuestions.markingMdxZh:
1 分：用角色与可访问名称来查询，而不是用类名。
1 分：执行用户动作（点击）并断言可见结果。
1 分：说明测试现在能熬过改名，并且能抓住 “总价不再更新” 的问题。

questions.title: The page the crawler sees as empty
questions.contentMdx:
A content page is a client-rendered single-page app: the server sends a shell whose only body content is `
`, and the text appears only after the JavaScript has downloaded and run. With JavaScript blocked (or before it finishes on a slow phone) the page looks empty, and the fetched HTML source contains none of the article. `source.png` shows the raw HTML the server returned.
questions.contentMdxZh:
一个内容页是客户端渲染的单页应用：服务器返回的骨架里，body 内容只有一个 `
`，正文要等 JavaScript 下载并执行之后才会出现。在禁用 JavaScript（或在慢手机上 JS 还没跑完）时，页面看上去是空的，而取回的 HTML 源码里完全没有正文内容。`source.png` 展示了服务器返回的原始 HTML。

subQuestions.label: (a)
subQuestions.questionMdx: Why is the page empty before the JavaScript runs, and what does that mean for a crawler that does not run JavaScript?
subQuestions.answerMdx: This is client-side rendering: the HTML the server sends is only a shell with an empty container, and the actual content is created in the browser by JavaScript after it loads. Until that script runs there is nothing in the DOM to show, so the user sees a blank page. Anything that reads the HTML without running the app's JavaScript — such as a crawler or a link-preview generator — sees only the empty shell, not the article.
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for stating the server sends only an empty shell and the content is built by JavaScript in the browser.
1 mark for stating that without running that JavaScript there is no content, so anything reading the HTML sees an empty page.
subQuestions.questionMdxZh: 为什么在 JavaScript 运行之前页面是空的？对不执行 JavaScript 的爬虫来说这意味着什么？
subQuestions.answerMdxZh: 这是客户端渲染：服务器发来的 HTML 只是一个带空容器的骨架，真正的内容要等 JavaScript 加载后在浏览器里生成。脚本运行之前，DOM 里没有可显示的东西，所以用户看到空白页。任何不执行该应用 JavaScript 的读取者——例如爬虫或链接预览生成器——看到的都只是空骨架，而不是正文。
subQuestions.markingMdxZh:
1 分：说明服务器只发来空骨架，内容由浏览器里的 JavaScript 生成。
1 分：说明不运行这段 JavaScript 就没有内容，读取 HTML 的一方只会看到空页面。

subQuestions.label: (b)
subQuestions.questionMdx: Explain how SSR and SSG differ from CSR in where and when the HTML is produced, and one trade-off of each.
subQuestions.answerMdx: With SSR the HTML is produced on the server for each request: the server runs the components and returns filled HTML, which then rehydrates into the interactive app in the browser — trade-off: it costs server work on every request and needs a server running. With SSG the HTML is produced once at build time and the same static file is served to everyone — trade-off: it is fast and cheap to serve, but the page is fixed at build time unless you rebuild, so it suits content that rarely changes. Both send real content in the first response, unlike CSR where content appears only after JavaScript runs.
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for SSR: HTML produced per request on the server (with rehydration).
1 mark for SSG: HTML produced once at build time and served as a static file.
1 mark for one trade-off of each (SSR: per-request server cost; SSG: content fixed until rebuild).
subQuestions.questionMdxZh: 请说明 SSR、SSG 与 CSR 在 “HTML 在哪、何时生成” 上的区别，并各给一个取舍。
subQuestions.answerMdxZh: SSR 在每个请求时于服务器生成 HTML：服务器运行组件并返回填好内容的 HTML，随后在浏览器里水合（rehydrate）成可交互的应用——取舍：每个请求都消耗服务器算力，并且需要一个常驻的服务器。SSG 在构建时一次性生成 HTML，之后把同一份静态文件发给所有人——取舍：托管快且便宜，但页面在构建时就固定了，除非重新构建，因此适合很少变化的内容。两者都会在首个响应里带上真实内容，而 CSR 要等 JavaScript 运行后才出现内容。
subQuestions.markingMdxZh:
1 分：SSR——每次请求在服务器生成 HTML（并水合）。
1 分：SSG——构建时一次性生成，作为静态文件分发。
1 分：各一个取舍（SSR：每请求服务器开销；SSG：内容在重新构建前固定）。

subQuestions.label: (c)
subQuestions.questionMdx: Choose the right strategy for a marketing page whose content barely changes, and justify it.
subQuestions.answerMdx: Use SSG. The page's HTML can be generated once at build time and reused for every visitor, so the first response already contains the full content and needs no JavaScript to be readable — good for crawlers and slow devices. Because the content barely changes, the usual downside of SSG (having to rebuild to update) rarely applies, and there is no per-request server-rendering cost.
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for choosing SSG.
1 mark for justifying it with prebuilt HTML served to everyone (readable without JavaScript).
1 mark for connecting the choice to the content barely changing, so the rebuild downside rarely matters.
subQuestions.questionMdxZh: 对于一个内容几乎不变的营销页面，请选择合适策略并给出理由。
subQuestions.answerMdxZh: 选 SSG。这个页面的 HTML 可以在构建时一次性生成、给每个访客复用，因此首个响应里就带着完整内容，不依赖 JavaScript 也能阅读——对爬虫和慢设备都友好。由于内容几乎不变，SSG 通常的缺点（更新需要重新构建）几乎不构成问题，而且没有每次请求都渲染的服务端开销。
subQuestions.markingMdxZh:
1 分：选择 SSG。
1 分：以 “预构建的 HTML 分发给所有人、无需 JavaScript 即可阅读” 作为理由。
1 分：把这一选择与 “内容几乎不变，因此重新构建的缺点几乎不影响” 联系起来。

questions.title: Lint switched off, bug shipped
questions.contentMdx: A student could not get the linter to pass, so they disabled it and kept coding. `npm run build` still succeeded, they submitted, and a review found a comparison written with `==` and a variable that was never used. `terminal.png` shows a green build next to a skipped lint step.
questions.contentMdxZh: 一位同学搞不定 linter 报错，于是把它关掉继续写代码。`npm run build` 依然成功，他就提交了；结果在评审中发现了一处用 `==` 写的比较，以及一个从未被使用的变量。`terminal.png` 展示了构建通过、lint 步骤被跳过的情形。

subQuestions.label: (a)
subQuestions.questionMdx: Why does turning lint off not stop the build, and what kind of problems does that let through?
subQuestions.answerMdx: Linting and building are separate steps. The build only needs the code to compile and bundle, so nothing runs the linter and the build still succeeds. Disabling lint lets through code-quality and hazard problems that are still valid JavaScript — for example a `==` comparison that coerces unexpectedly, an unused or misspelled variable, or a suspicious pattern — none of which make the build fail on their own.
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for stating lint and build are separate steps, so the build does not run the linter.
1 mark for giving the kind of problems that survive (valid-but-risky code such as `==` or an unused variable).
subQuestions.questionMdxZh: 为什么关掉 lint 并不会让构建失败？这又会放过哪些问题？
subQuestions.answerMdxZh: lint 与构建是两个独立的步骤。构建只要求代码能编译、能打包，所以没人会去跑 linter，构建照样成功。关掉 lint 就会放过那些仍然是合法 JavaScript 的代码质量与风险问题——例如会意外做类型转换的 `==` 比较、未使用或拼错的变量、以及可疑的写法——这些本身都不会让构建失败。
subQuestions.markingMdxZh:
1 分：说明 lint 与构建是独立步骤，构建不会运行 linter。
1 分：给出会漏过去的问题类型（合法但有风险的代码，如 `==` 或未使用变量）。

subQuestions.label: (b)
subQuestions.questionMdx: Explain what lint is for versus what the build does.
subQuestions.answerMdx: Lint is static analysis of source code: it reads the code without running it and flags patterns against a set of rules (style, common mistakes, likely bugs), quickly and per-line. The build compiles and bundles: it resolves imports, transforms JSX and produces the output files; it fails on hard errors such as a missing module or a syntax error, but it does not judge style or suspicious-but-legal patterns. Lint catches "this is legal but probably wrong"; the build catches "this cannot be turned into a working app".
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for describing lint as static analysis that flags risky patterns without running the code.
1 mark for describing the build as resolving imports and producing output, failing on hard errors (missing module, syntax error).
1 mark for the contrast: lint finds legal-but-wrong patterns; the build finds what cannot be compiled at all.
subQuestions.questionMdxZh: 请说明 lint 的用途，以及构建做的是什么。
subQuestions.answerMdxZh: lint 是对源码的静态分析：它不运行代码，只按一套规则（风格、常见错误、可疑 Bug）快速逐行检查并标出问题。构建则负责编译与打包：解析 import、转换 JSX、产出输出文件；它会在硬错误上失败，例如找不到模块或语法错误，但它不会评判风格，也不会判断 “合法但可疑” 的写法。lint 抓的是 “这合法但大概率是错的”；构建抓的是 “这根本没法变成能跑的应用”。
subQuestions.markingMdxZh:
1 分：把 lint 描述为不运行代码、只标出风险模式的静态分析。
1 分：把构建描述为解析 import 并产出产物，遇到硬错误（缺模块、语法错误）就失败。
1 分：给出对比——lint 抓 “合法但写错”，构建抓 “根本编译不出来”。

subQuestions.label: (c)
subQuestions.questionMdx: Give one case only lint catches and one case only the build catches, and explain why you keep both.
subQuestions.answerMdx: Only lint: a `==` where `===` was meant, or an unused variable — the code runs and the build is happy, but the pattern is a hazard lint flags. Only the build: an `import` of a file that does not exist, or a syntax error — no lint rule can produce a bundle, and the build fails because it cannot resolve or compile. Keep both because they cover different failures: lint guards the correctness and consistency of the source before it runs, the build proves the app can actually be produced and served. Turning lint off to silence it hides the first class of bugs without fixing them.
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for a case only lint catches (e.g. `==` misuse, unused variable).
1 mark for a case only the build catches (e.g. a missing import, a syntax error).
1 mark for explaining both are kept because they catch different failures and silencing lint hides bugs rather than fixing them.
subQuestions.questionMdxZh: 请各举一个 “只有 lint 能抓” 和 “只有构建能抓” 的例子，并解释为什么要两者都保留。
subQuestions.answerMdxZh: 只有 lint 能抓：本想写 `===` 却写成 `==`，或未使用的变量——代码能跑、构建也开心，但这个模式是 lint 会标记的隐患。只有构建能抓：import 了一个并不存在的文件，或出现语法错误——没有任何 lint 规则能产出打包文件，构建因为无法解析或编译而失败。两者都要保留，因为它们覆盖的是不同的失败：lint 在代码运行前守住它的正确性与一致性，构建则证明这个应用确实能被产出并交付。为了消掉报错而关掉 lint，只是把第一类 Bug 藏起来，并没有修好。
subQuestions.markingMdxZh:
1 分：举出只有 lint 能抓的例子（如 `==` 误用、未使用变量）。
1 分：举出只有构建能抓的例子（如缺失 import、语法错误）。
1 分：说明两者保留是因为覆盖不同失败，且关掉 lint 只是隐藏 Bug 而非修复。
